channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Approves Public Works for Repeated Waste Violations
item.description: The Jogorku Kenesh approved amendments to the Code of Offenses, introducing public works for repeat offenders of waste disposal and cleanliness rules. First-time offenders face a warning or fines. Repeat violations within a year, such as illegal dumping or burning of waste after a prior fine, will result in 20-30 hours of public work.

item.title: Tajikistan Delegation Attends 70th IAEA General Conference in Vienna
item.description: A delegation from Tajikistan is participating in the 70th General Conference of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in Vienna, running from September 14-18. The delegation is led by Deputy Foreign Minister Nigina Alizoda and includes officials from the Ministry of Industry and New Technologies and the National Academy of Sciences. Discussions will focus on the safe and peaceful use of nuclear technologies.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Proposes Joint Medical Center and Easier Visa Rules with South Korea
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov proposed establishing a joint medical center in Kyrgyzstan and easing visa regulations with South Korea during talks with his South Korean counterpart. Discussions also covered trade, investment, and infrastructure projects. Japarov invited the South Korean president to visit Kyrgyzstan, suggesting timing it with the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations.

item.title: Uzbekistan introduces "5+1" medical bachelor's program, abolishes narrow specialization master's
item.description: Uzbekistan is introducing a six-year "5+1" general medical bachelor's program based on the "Treatment of Diseases" specialty. Graduates will receive a general practitioner qualification and can work as family doctors. The master's programs for narrow specializations are being abolished.

item.title: Part of Bishkek to experience 10-hour water supply suspension on September 17
item.description: A section of Bishkek will be without drinking water from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. on September 17 due to maintenance at the Airport water intake facility. The outage will affect the old airport area, Chingiz Aitmatov Avenue, and nearby streets, impacting residential buildings, schools, and healthcare facilities.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP Proposes International Committee for World Nomad Games
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan, Tabyldy Muratbekov, has proposed the creation of an international committee for the World Nomad Games. He stated that the games have become a key feature of Kyrgyzstan, increasing international interest in the country. The proposed committee aims to systematically promote the history, culture, and national sports of nomadic peoples worldwide.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP Demands Urgent Inspection of School Coal Quality Amid Safety Concerns
item.description: Kyrgyzstan MP Tabyldy Muratbekov has called for an urgent inspection of coal supplied to schools after instances of spontaneous combustion were reported. He noted that poor coal quality or other factors could pose a safety risk. Muratbekov urged for laboratory analysis of the fuel and prevention of hazardous coal delivery to schools.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Bahrain Discuss Launching Direct Flights Between Tashkent and Manama
item.description: Uzbekistan and Bahrain are discussing the possibility of launching direct flights between Tashkent and Manama. The issue was addressed during a meeting between the Chairman of the Uzbekistan Tourism Committee and the Minister of Tourism of Bahrain. Both sides also agreed to enhance mutual tourist flows and strengthen direct ties between tourism industry representatives.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan border guards honored at Ata-Beyit memorial complex
item.description: A ceremony was held at the Ata-Beyit memorial complex to honor military personnel who died defending the state border during clashes on the Kyrgyz-Tajik section in 2021 and 2022. The State Border Service reported that approximately 100 people died on the Kyrgyz side in these conflicts.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP highlights school readiness issues and textbook shortages
item.description: A Member of Parliament has raised concerns about some schools' unreadiness for the new academic year, citing one school's shift to online learning due to unfinished renovations. The MP also questioned why parents must buy textbooks, despite significant annual funding for their publication.

item.title: Zelenskyy: Russian drones flew twice near his plane over Moldova
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russian drones flew twice near his aircraft while it was over Moldova. He described the incident as a near-miss encounter with a drone.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Six-Year "5+1" Bachelor's Degree in Medicine from 2027/28
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce a six-year "5+1" bachelor's degree in medicine starting from the 2027/2028 academic year. The program will include a full year of practical training for final-year students. The Ministry of Health will approve state order parameters based on current and future needs for medical personnel.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Meets South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon met with South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo in Seoul. They discussed expanding bilateral cooperation in industry, energy, agriculture, transport, finance, and digitalization. Both sides expressed interest in strengthening economic and investment ties and activating joint mechanisms.

item.title: Tajikistan President Emomali Rahmon Holds High-Level Talks in South Korea
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon met with South Korean leadership in Seoul on September 16 during an official visit. Discussions focused on strengthening bilateral cooperation, with both sides emphasizing historical ties and shared values. Priority areas for collaboration include trade, economy, investment, energy, transport, digitalization, agriculture, and tourism.

item.title: Dushanbe Discusses Satellite Communications Development with Chinese Specialists
item.description: Dushanbe hosted a meeting between specialists from Tajikistan's Communications Service and Chinese experts from the China Academy of Space Technology and other companies. The discussion focused on developing satellite communications, implementing modern space technologies, and enhancing technical exchange to improve Tajikistan's telecommunications sector.

item.title: Korea and Kyrgyzstan Elevate Relations to Comprehensive Partnership
item.description: Bilateral relations between the Republic of Korea and the Kyrgyz Republic reached a new level in December 2024, becoming a comprehensive partnership. Cooperation now spans development aid, trade, investment, digital transformation, and climate action, building on existing exchanges.

item.title: Khorezm Region to Attract $100 Million Investment for Waste-to-Energy Project
item.description: The Khorezm region will attract $100 million in investments for a project to generate electricity from waste. "Uzenergosotish" will purchase the electricity produced under the project for 30 years with guaranteed terms.

item.title: China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan Railway to Boost Eurasian Trade
item.description: The construction of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is a key event for Central Asia, according to Mukhtor Umarov, Chairman of the Uzbekistan Economic Assembly. He stated that connecting this line with the Middle Corridor and the Trans-Afghan route will significantly shorten logistics and position Uzbekistan as a major Eurasian trade hub.

item.title: Biosecurity Crucial for Central Asia Amid Global Changes, Expert Says
item.description: Kairat Tabyanov, a virologist and biosecurity specialist at the Regional Environmental Center for Central Asia (CAREC), emphasizes the growing importance of biosecurity due to global changes and trade. He focuses on zoonoses, infections transferable from animals to humans, and consults on a World Bank project related to veterinary biosecurity.

item.title: One Health Approach Strengthens Regional Cooperation in Central Asia
item.description: Pierre Gerber, a senior agricultural economist at the World Bank, discussed the 'One Health' approach at a Bishkek conference, aiming to balance economic development with health and ecosystem security in Central Asia. The initiative promotes intersectoral cooperation, project implementation, and scientific exchange to address transboundary risks like infectious diseases.

item.title: Uzbekistan plans to establish Biome Center in cooperation with South Korea
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea have signed a memorandum to establish a Biome Center, based at the Center of Advanced Technologies of the Academy of Sciences. The center will focus on cell technologies for treating diseases like cancer and regenerating tissues, utilizing bioinformatics and AI.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman to Jointly Combat Environmental Challenges
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman will cooperate on environmental challenges, including water scarcity and decarbonization. During Oman Climate Week, Uzbek delegates met with Omani officials to discuss expanding practical cooperation. Uzbekistan is interested in Oman's experience with water desalination and groundwater management.

item.title: Uzbek President meets with compatriots in South Korea
item.description: During a state visit to South Korea, Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Uzbek citizens working and studying there. Discussions covered reforms in Uzbekistan, proposals for economic and educational ties, integrating AI and Korean digital technologies, and strengthening cultural-humanitarian connections.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Build $100 Million Waste-to-Energy Plant in Khorezm
item.description: A $100 million waste-to-energy plant is planned for construction in Uzbekistan's Khorezm region. South Korean company Green Hammer Co., Ltd. will invest in the facility, designed to process 800 tons of waste daily and generate 71 million kWh of electricity annually. The project is scheduled for implementation between 2026 and 2028.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea: Strategic Partnership Figures Highlight Trade Imbalance
item.description: Trade between Uzbekistan and South Korea reached $1.1 billion in January-July, with Uzbekistan's exports at $37.5 million and imports from South Korea at $1.037 billion. This imbalance is attributed to Uzbekistan's demand for high-tech equipment. South Korea invested $216.4 million in Uzbekistan during January-June, with 730 Korean-capitalized enterprises operating in the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Discusses Airport Cooperation with South Korean Firm
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Kim Beom Ho, acting president of Incheon International Airport Corporation, in South Korea. They discussed modernizing Urgench airport and building a new Tashkent airport. The Korean firm plans to open an office in Tashkent, potentially becoming a center for airport management and training.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Gradual Increase in Retirement Age
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Economy and Finance has proposed gradually increasing the retirement age from 60 to 63 for men and from 55 to 58 for women. The plan involves a three-month annual increase starting in 2028, aiming for completion by 2039. The proposal is currently open for public discussion until September 30.

item.title: Tax Committee generated 72% of budget revenues in first half of 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan's budget revenues reached 277 trillion soms in the first half of 2026, a 63 trillion som increase year-on-year. The Tax Committee generated 72% (149 trillion soms), and the Customs Committee 20% (41 trillion soms). Corporate income tax revenue grew significantly due to higher commodity prices and improved enterprise performance.

item.title: Uzbekistan allocates 229 billion soms for child vaccinations in six months
item.description: Uzbekistan spent approximately 23 trillion soms on healthcare in the first six months of 2026. Of this, 229 billion soms were allocated for child vaccinations, immunizing 1.4 million children against 13 infectious diseases. Significant funds also went to medical staff salaries, medicines, and hospital construction.

item.title: Karakol Municipal Transport Fleet Expanded with New Buses
item.description: Karakol has introduced new modern buses equipped with air conditioning for its city and suburban routes. The mayor inspected the transport, which now includes over 50 updated buses serving 15 lines. An additional 63 buses are expected, enhancing public transport coverage.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ministry of Internal Affairs Investigates Charity Fund Fraud Case
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs is investigating a fraud case involving the 'Biz el menen' charity fund. The fund's leader was arrested for allegedly collecting large sums of money through fraudulent activities, with preliminary damages estimated at 30 million soms between 2024 and 2026.

item.title: Kyrgyz Students at GITIS Face Housing Issues; Ministry of Culture Intervenes
item.description: Students from Kyrgyzstan studying at the Russian Institute of Theatre Arts (GITIS) are facing housing problems due to dormitory repairs. The Ministry of Culture is taking measures to ensure their accommodation. The issue is under the personal control of the Minister of Culture.

item.title: Pregnant Woman Dies in Surxondaryo Due to Negligence of Surgeons
item.description: A pregnant woman died in Surxondaryo due to the negligence of surgeons. She had visited doctors twice, who gave different diagnoses and failed to identify intestinal obstruction. Her condition worsened, leading to her death and that of her fetus.

item.title: Tajikistan: Authorities explain student abuse case, new US sanctions on Iran discussed
item.description: Authorities in Tajikistan have commented on a case of student abuse by a teacher. Discussions also covered potential impacts of new US sanctions on Iran's relations with Dushanbe. Other news includes tourism figures to Uzbekistan and public transport improvements.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Court investigation begins in 'Real Sanjik' case, new details revealed
item.description: A court investigation has commenced in the 'Real Sanjik' case, with new details emerging. During the first court session on September 14, an audio recording presented by the accused, Sanjar Karimov, was played. The recording featured a conversation between Feruza Rahmatullayeva, her husband, two lawyers, and Karimov.

item.title: President Saparov arrives in South Korea for official visit and summit
item.description: President Saparov has arrived in the Republic of Korea for an official visit. He was met at the airport by South Korean officials. The visit includes bilateral meetings with the leadership and participation in the first Central Asia + Republic of Korea summit and a business summit.

item.title: State audit finds $25 million loan to company linked to Tashiev was 'ineffectively' issued
item.description: The Accounts Chamber stated that the state 'ineffectively' issued a $25 million loan to a fuel company associated with former GKNB head Kamchybek Tashiev. The firm belongs to Akylbek Mamatov, whose family has won state tenders for fuel supply for 10 years.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Competence Center for Airport Management with South Korean Partner
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to establish an airport management competence center in Tashkent, operated by South Korea's Incheon International Airport Corporation (IIAC). The center will focus on airport management, digitalization, and personnel training. IIAC is already involved in modernizing Urgench airport and building a new Tashkent international airport.
